state: Scenario v is a scenario where the project activity of converting the area to a protected forest would be performed without being registered as the VCS AFOLU project. This scenario faces financial barriers.

There are no barriers preventing this scenario from occurring and therefore scenario iv. (combination of Natural Forest Management and the Mosaic Planting Approach) is considered as the most likely baseline scenario for this project.

Other formerly Class II Forest Reserves (e.g. Ulu Segama and Malua) have primarily been protected because of external financial incentives; Therefore the outcome of the common practice analysis is that the project activity, without the prospect of the sale of GHG credits, is not common practice.
Following the steps above, it is concluded that the proposed VCS AFOLU project activity is not the baseline scenario and, hence, it is additional

state: The project has sought to identify all stakeholders with a relationship to the project and to undertake an assessment of their rights, interests and relevance to the project itself.
Since the inception of community engagements in late 2017, the project has held a total of 11 community workshops and dialogue sessions, attended by a combined total of 488 community participants.
The project is currently in the process of formalising redress mechanisms for any potential grievances arising from project zone communities or other stakeholders.

Human-induced risks to the project’s biodiversity benefits, both in the short and long-term, are essentially the same to those related to climate change benefits (above) as they relate to the protection and regeneration of the natural ecosystem.
